issues.failure_explanation: Every convergence result (Propositions prop:descent–prop:til2, Lemmas lem:LSbase–lem:square:summable, Theorems thm:globalconverg–thm:globalconverg:M) assumes y^n exactly solves the subproblem, using its optimality condition (eq:subpro:optcon). Proposition prop:proximal_to_pre shows only that a single preconditioned iteration with M = Mbd - T reproduces such an exact solve. For two or more inner iterations the computed y^n satisfies no subproblem optimality condition with any stated PSD weight, and no analysis of the multi-iteration case appears anywhere; the paper nevertheless repeatedly promises the guarantee ('we will prove', 'we can guarantee') and implements 50 Jacobi iterations per outer step in the experiments. The claim is in fact provable for Mbd >= T (a k-fold Richardson sweep with fixed Mbd equals one exact proximal step with a PSD weight M_k), but that argument is absent, so the promise is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: It is important to note that we will prove that any finite and feasible preconditioned iterations can ensure the global convergence of the whole nonlinear second-order convex splitting method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma showing that k >= 1 preconditioned iterations (Richardson/SGS/Jacobi with Mbd >= T, T = (2/dt)I + A) started from the current point produce exactly the minimizer of the subproblem with the PSD weight M_k (in Mbd^{-1/2}-symmetrized coordinates M_k is a rational function of Mbd^{-1/2}T Mbd^{-1/2} with nonnegative spectrum when Mbd >= T), and invoke the existing analysis with M = M_k; alternatively restrict all claims to exact subproblem solves or single preconditioned iterations, explicitly excluding the 50-iteration implementations.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee - global convergence with inexact inner solves and no error control - is not established by the paper's analysis; the numerically implemented algorithms (50 Jacobi iterations per subproblem solve) are not covered by any stated result.
issues.title: Unproven claim that any finite number of preconditioned inner iterations preserves global convergence
issues.why_classification: The claim is central (abstract, introduction, Section 2.1) and unsupported as written; a complete repair exists but requires a new contained nontrivial lemma, or a scope restriction removing coverage of the implemented algorithms - more than a routine local edit, but no major loss or new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence theory requires the accepted step to satisfy 0 <= lambda_n < sqrt(4/(3*dt*L) - 1/2) - 1 (Theorem thm:globalconverg; the bound is even smaller in Theorem thm:square:sum:til), and line-search feasibility needs 0 < alpha < 2/(3*dt) - L (Lemma lem:LSbase, Corollary coro:til1). Algorithm 1 imposes neither: the input lambda_max > 0 is unconstrained (and Step 6 actually uses an unconstrained bar-lambda_max, with no cap on the accepted step), and alpha > 0 is unconstrained. With the paper's own experimental values (dt = 6 - 1e-15, L = 1/9) the theoretical bound is sqrt(1.5) - 1 < 0.225, while the line search starts at bar-lambda_max = 5; hence Algorithm 1 as specified - and as run - can accept steps far outside the regime covered by Theorems thm:globalconverg, thm:square:sum:til and thm:globalconverg:M, and for large alpha the Step-6 loop may never satisfy the Armijo condition.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised global convergence guarantee does not follow for Algorithm 1 as stated; the 'aggressive' large-step regime used in all reported experiments is not covered by the theory.

Moreover Lambda(i) = 2y(i) - 1 takes negative values whenever y(i) < 1/2 (e.g. y(i) = 0 for negative-prior pixels), making the prior term -(eta/2)(u(i)-y(i))^2 concave, so H - assumed convex throughout the analysis (needed for the strong convexity of H^n in Propositions prop:descent and prop:til:1) - is nonconvex (its Hessian is negative on constant vectors).
